Presidential debates aren't actual debates any more.

They used to be. Lincoln and Douglas is the best example--those men argued with each other, point and counterpoint, raising issues and asking each other all kinds of awkward questions for 5 or 6 debates around the nation.

Now they're basically PR appearances, a chance to make a 60-second statement that can be turned into sound bites (both pro and anti) the day after. There's no real discussion of anything, just talking points.

I'd love to see a series of ACTUAL, REAL, ONE-ON-ONE DEBATES between the candidates....but then I'm a political geek. I understand why networks don't do this any more, but they certainly shouldn't call what they DO today "debates".
